1: # Minimal translation from accepted NL0
2: 
3: Start with the accepted source map and specification. Read the supplied proof
4: and definitions where needed to choose faithful types. Other Yui documents,
5: library searches and individual background notes are available on demand;
6: there is no requirement to preload the entire skill or all note bodies.
7: 
8: 1. Preserve the accepted source and Audit A. Use a source revision only when an
9:    actual mathematical change or useful shared extraction requires it. Reusing
10:    unchanged acceptance runs integrity checks, not another model Audit A.
11: 2. Choose the mathematical representation, complete original H/E input types,
12:    N/P output types and useful local proof obligations. The controller copies
13:    source paragraphs and note locations. Mathlib is freely available; retain an
14:    M port only when useful, otherwise apply the library directly. Supply short
15:    `endpoint_correspondence` notes for every E and complete P (including all
16:    hypotheses), explaining direct or equivalent translation. Save partial interface drafts, revise
17:    those drafts, and use small Lean probes for uncertain types. Do not restart
18:    from an empty interface after an ordinary error.
19: 3. Type-check source correspondence, dependency boundaries and the complete
20:    interface, then obtain a separate independent semantic interface review.
21:    Normal full/translation entry dispatches no proof worker before its actual
22:    hash-bound receipt passes. Repair located failures with the interface author
23:    and have the same separate reviewer assess changed output. Final machine Audit B
24:    inherits that review only if the actual complete artifact preserves the freeze. The
25:    lower-level legacy mechanical freeze can record `PENDING_AUDIT_B`; it does
26:    not satisfy this normal-workflow pre-proof gate.
27: 4. Run local proof workers on frozen conditional obligations. Each gets its
28:    input statements, matched source paragraphs and own compact note index.
29:    Read a full note only if useful. No sibling proof bodies, other cases,
30:    developer history or additional personal skills are supplied.
31:    Use [Lean implementation safeguards](lean-writing.md) for library
32:    applications and conversions, including small type checks in preparation.
33:    Yui proof workers receive these requirements in their stage instructions.
34: 5. Attempt mechanical [assembly](assembly.md) and complete native inspection.
35:    Use the serial connection author only for real connection/library-discharge
36:    repair under unchanged E/P/definitions. Normal final Audit B is machine-only:
37:    inherit the actual pre-proof semantics after checking full endpoint types,
38:    defining header and complete closure. Only proof-valid interface drift opens
39:    B-final. Faithful drift is warning-qualified; a nonpass waits for the user's
40:    explicit delivery/recheck/translation-reset choice. Invalid proof is never
41:    semantically overridden.
42: 
43: ## Background notes are references, not extra ports
44: 
45: New contracts select `source.background_mode: node_local_reference`. Original
46: H/E/M/N/P entries remain unchanged; Audit A's verified supplement remains
47: hash-bound. Do not turn every note into a new M root, retype its entire library
48: signature, or require an extra theorem merely to restate it. The frozen
49: stage-one text's historical `background.effective` expansion is still supported
50: as `promoted_inputs` for old contracts; it is not the new translation default.
51: 
52: At the pre-freeze semantic review and final Audit B, notes are guidance, not library permissions. All proved results in
53: the pinned Mathlib environment are available without registration. Review every
54: external E and complete P against its actual Lean type using the concise author
55: correspondence explanation; independently check direct or equivalent meaning.
56: A new external assumption or stronger hypothesis still returns to the source
57: boundary. See [the complete Audit B standard](audit-b.md).
58: 
59: ## Work continuously, report genuine blockers
60: 
61: There is no ordinary `TASK_INCOMPLETE` reporting tool. While unfinished, keep
62: making concrete edits, queries or proof checks. Submit a completed artifact or
63: report a supported mathematical/source/input blocker. If a model turn ends
64: without either, the controller sends one short continuation instruction; it
65: does not demand a progress essay. State/usage recording is programmatic.
66: Proof workers follow [structured diagnosis and repair](proof-repair.md): report
67: actual packet obstructions. Progress counters are passive; no idle-turn count
68: cancels sibling work or authorizes interface changes.
69: 
70: Whole-case/stage execution, total tokens and calls are unlimited by default.
71: Each native check has the configured 180-second wall limit and finite Lean
72: heartbeat policy. Keep measuring usage and allow explicit
73: cancellation. Only a user-requested finite case deadline covers the entire
74: translation, including preparation, queue waiting, parallel proofs, assembly
75: and Audit B; later stages cannot reset that optional deadline. Preserve partial
76: results and report execution health separately from mathematical acceptance.

value.full_target:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
value.conclusion: For every real t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝⁿ, the finite energy E is differentiable at t, and E'(t)=0. Here e=|u_t|²+∑_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|² and E(t)=∫_{ℝⁿ}e(x,t) dx with Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure; there is no assertion at time zero.

hypotheses.statement: u is jointly C∞ on ℝⁿ×(0,∞).
q∈ℝᵐ satisfies |q|=1 for the Euclidean norm.
For every x∈ℝⁿ and t>0, |u(x,t)|=1 for the Euclidean norm.
For every x∈ℝⁿ and t>0 there exists a real scalar a such that u_tt(x,t)−Δ_x u(x,t)=a u(x,t), with Δ_x u=∑_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u componentwise. No regularity or global choice of the scalar is assumed.
For every pair of real numbers 0<s<t<∞ there exists a compact C⊆ℝⁿ such that u(x,r)=q for every x∉C and every r∈[s,t].

definitions.definition: Space = Fin n → ℝ, the fixed standard coordinates on ℝⁿ, with its product norm, Borel structure and topology.
Value = Fin m → ℝ, the fixed standard coordinates on ℝᵐ, with its product norm and topology.
For v,w∈Value, dot(v,w)=∑_{k∈Fin m} v(k)w(k). This is the Euclidean dot product.
For v∈Value, normSq(v)=dot(v,v), the Euclidean norm squared.
In the fixed standard coordinates, ubar(x,t)=u(x,t) for t>0 and ubar(x,t)=q for t≤0. This is a total representative only; its definition asserts no regularity at t=0.

definitions.type: open-domain notation: subset of Space × ℝ
definitions.definition: U={(x,t)∈Space×ℝ:0<t}. All calculus assertions about ubar are restricted to U.
For j∈Fin n, basis(j)=Pi.single j 1 is the standard vector with coordinate 1 at j and 0 elsewhere.

definitions.type: notation for calculus, topology and measure
definitions.definition: AnalyticNotation fixes the following typed conventions, with each function, space, point and measure supplied by its own statement or local scope. D and fderiv denote the Fréchet derivative over the field specified at each use, defaulting to ℝ; deriv is the corresponding one-variable derivative. The total derivative operators return zero when a derivative does not exist. HasDerivAt relates a one-variable function, its derivative value and its basepoint. ContDiffOn and ContDiffAt express the indicated C-order regularity on a set or at a point; ∞ means all finite orders and ω means analytic. minSmoothness at order 2 is 2 for a field satisfying IsRCLikeNormedField and ω otherwise; IsSymmSndFDerivAt means that the second Fréchet derivative at the specified point is symmetric in its two direction arguments. 𝓝 denotes the neighborhood filter. The support of a function is the set where its value is nonzero, tsupport is the closure of that set, and HasCompactSupport means this closure is compact. ContinuousOn means continuity relative to the indicated set. AEStronglyMeasurable means agreement almost everywhere with a strongly measurable function. Integrable means ae strong measurability and finite integral of the norm; IntegrableOn means integrability with respect to the restriction of the specified measure to the specified set. The Bochner integral uses the total library convention; for real integrable functions it is the ordinary finite Lebesgue integral. A set indicator equals its function on that set and zero off it. An ae assertion holds outside a null set for the indicated measure. The extended norm on an ESeminormedAddMonoid is denoted by ‖·‖ₑ; real numbers have finite extended norm. Standard structure names retain their usual mathematical meanings: OpensMeasurableSpace says that open sets are measurable, BorelSpace identifies the measurable structure with the Borel structure, IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts says compact sets have finite measure, and IsAddHaarMeasure means an additive Haar measure. These conventions define notation and assert no application theorem.
V(x,t)_k=deriv (r↦ubar(x,r)_k) t, for each x,t and k∈Fin m.
A(x,t)_k=deriv (r↦V(x,r)_k) t.
Psp(j,x,t)_k=fderiv ℝ (y↦ubar(y,t)_k) x (basis(j)).
Ssp(j,x,t)_k=fderiv ℝ (y↦Psp(j,y,t)_k) x (basis(j)).
L(x,t)=∑_{j∈Fin n} Ssp(j,x,t), the componentwise spatial Laplacian.

dx is canonical Lebesgue volume on Space: the product of the usual real Lebesgue measures in its fixed standard coordinates. It is the original dx on ℝⁿ. Spatial integrals without a displayed measure use dx.
e(x,t)=normSq(V(x,t))+∑_{j∈Fin n} normSq(Psp(j,x,t)). This is |u_t|²+∑_j |∂_{x_j}u|² at positive times, with the Euclidean/Frobenius squares and coefficient 1 on each term.
E(t)=∫_{Space} e(x,t) dx, using the total integral convention until integrability is proved. At positive times when integrable this is the original finite energy integral.
W(j,x,t)_k=fderiv ℝ (y↦V(y,t)_k) x (basis(j)).
d(x,t)=2 dot(V(x,t),A(x,t))+2∑_{j∈Fin n} dot(Psp(j,x,t),W(j,x,t)).

value.representation_notes: Preserve the prepared-basis lean_header verbatim. Space n and Value m are standard real coordinate tuples with product norm for their topology and Fréchet calculus; the physical Euclidean square is the explicit finite sum normSq, never the product norm square. The original map parameter u has domain Space n × Set.Ioi 0, and ubar u q extends it by q at nonpositive times exactly as D005. Smooth is ContDiffOn on the open half-space. The smoothness exponent ∞ is ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), strictly distinguished from analytic ω=(⊤ : WithTop ℕ∞). Derivatives are real scalar-coordinate deriv/fderiv and the mixed field uses the same spatial basis Pi.single j 1. iteratedFDeriv ℝ ell denotes the ell-fold continuous multilinear spacetime derivative, ell a positive natural. volume on Fin n→ℝ is canonical coordinate product Lebesgue measure, without scaling. The function-space submodule span encodes exactly finite real linear combinations of the listed sections. FirstCalculus, SecondCalculus, SlabVanishing and SupportedSection merely package explicit propositions, contain no asserted proof, and become available only when their T obligations are proved. No Audit A note is a premise. All M roots are omitted in favor of direct pinned library use; prepared native dependencies have port=null and there are no E roots.

steps.statement: FirstCalculus (ubar u q)
steps.explanation: Use the standard coordinate identity and affine time/spatial injections on the open positive half-space. Scalar coordinate projection and open-set derivative closure give smooth velocity and spatial fields and their actual first derivatives. The prepared product norm is used only for topology/calculus; dot and normSq retain the Euclidean metric. ContDiff exponents live in WithTop ℕ∞: the scoped ∞ is the embedded infinite natural, not the analytic top ω.

steps.statement: SecondCalculus (ubar u q)
steps.explanation: Differentiate the first-derivative evaluations along the same fixed injections. Apply second Fréchet derivative symmetry over ℝ to interchange the spatial and time directions. The pinned minSmoothness ℝ 2 equals 2 because ℝ is IsRCLikeNormedField; use the two-smoothness consequence of FirstCalculus. Iterate open-set derivative closure for smoothness of the second-order fields. Supply named field/order/set arguments when inference needs them.

steps.statement:
FirstCalculus (ubar u q) ∧ SecondCalculus (ubar u q) ∧
ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun p : Space n × ℝ => density (ubar u q) p.1 p.2) {p | 0 < p.2} ∧
ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun p : Space n × ℝ => densityRate (ubar u q) p.1 p.2) {p | 0 < p.2} ∧
(∀ (x : Space n) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → HasDerivAt (fun r => density (ubar u q) x r) (densityRate (ubar u q) x t) t) ∧
(∀ (j : Fin n) (x : Space n) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → ∀ k : Fin m,
 fderiv ℝ (fun y => (ubar u q) (y,t) k) x (Pi.single j 1) = spatial (ubar u q) j x t k ∧
 fderiv ℝ (fun y => velocity (ubar u q) y t k) x (Pi.single j 1) = mixed (ubar u q) j x t k ∧
 fderiv ℝ (fun y => spatial (ubar u q) j y t k) x (Pi.single j 1) = spatialSecond (ubar u q) j x t k) ∧
(∀ (x : Space n) (t : Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ)), (ubar u q) (x,t) = u (x,t)) ∧
(∀ (x : Space n) (t : ℝ), t ≤ 0 → (ubar u q) (x,t) = q)
steps.explanation: Export all of N001. Product differentiation of each squared coordinate and finite sums gives densityRate, with coefficient 2 in the derivative and coefficient 1 in density. Smoothness follows from finite products and sums. The three spatial equalities unfold the prepared definitions. Restriction/extension identities make the domain correspondence explicit; the Laplacian and energy are definitionally the specified finite sum and volume integral. No smoothness at zero is asserted.

steps.statement: ∀ t₀ : ℝ, 0 < t₀ → ∃ C : Set (Space n), SlabVanishing (ubar u q) q t₀ C
steps.explanation: Choose the compact set on [t₀/2,3t₀/2] from H006. Its complement times the open slab is open and ubar is locally constant there. Locality of the Fréchet derivative, iterated by induction, proves vanishing of every positive-order iteratedFDeriv; ell is a natural derivative order, with ell>0 excluding order zero. Restrict to the time/spatial sections to obtain all named zero fields and then the zero densities.

steps.statement:
(∀ t₀ : ℝ, 0 < t₀ → ∃ C : Set (Space n),
 SlabVanishing (ubar u q) q t₀ C ∧
 ∀ r ∈ Set.Ioo (t₀/2) (3*t₀/2),
 ∀ h ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (sections (ubar u q) r), SupportedSection C h) ∧
(∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → Integrable (fun x => density (ubar u q) x t))
steps.explanation: Export N002 with the same compact witness. sections lists exactly the source component sections, five scalar product families, energy density and its rate, and the five dot-product families. Submodule.span over ℝ means all finite real linear combinations, including the generators. Each section is continuous and zero off the closed compact C, so its topological support is contained in C, compact, and its integral is finite. Use direct library compact-support integrability, then closure under finite linear combinations. Since t₀ lies inside its slab, conclude integrability at every positive time.

steps.statement:
∀ t₀ : ℝ, 0 < t₀ →
 ∃ b : Space n → ℝ,
 (Set.Ioo (t₀-t₀/4) (t₀+t₀/4)) ∈ 𝓝 t₀ ∧ (Set.Ioo (t₀-t₀/4) (t₀+t₀/4)) ⊆ Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ) ∧
 (∀ᶠ r in 𝓝 t₀, AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => density (ubar u q) x r) volume) ∧
 Integrable (fun x => density (ubar u q) x t₀) ∧
 AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => densityRate (ubar u q) x t₀) volume ∧
 (∀ᵐ x ∂volume, ∀ r ∈ (Set.Ioo (t₀-t₀/4) (t₀+t₀/4)), ‖densityRate (ubar u q) x r‖ ≤ b x) ∧
 Integrable b ∧
 (∀ᵐ x ∂volume, ∀ r ∈ (Set.Ioo (t₀-t₀/4) (t₀+t₀/4)), HasDerivAt (fun a => density (ubar u q) x a) (densityRate (ubar u q) x r) r)
steps.explanation: Use η=t₀/4 and C from N002. Bound the continuous rate on compact C×[t₀−η,t₀+η]; take B=max(B₀,0) and b=C.indicator (fun _ => B). Compactness gives measurability and finite volume, hence integrability of b. Outside C the rate vanishes. Both bound and derivative predicates hold for every spatial x simultaneously for every r in s; pass these complete predicates to almost-everywhere statements without exchanging quantifiers. Continuity supplies the required measurability. All choices depend on t₀; there is no global uniform bound.

steps.statement: ∀ t₀ : ℝ, 0 < t₀ → HasDerivAt (energy (ubar u q)) (∫ x, densityRate (ubar u q) x t₀) t₀
steps.explanation: Export N003. Specialize the pinned dominated local derivative theorem to α=Space n, μ=volume, real parameter and codomain, F(r,x)=density v x r, F'(r,x)=densityRate v x r, and the s,b from T006. Its ae-first bound and derivative premises are supplied in precisely their declared order. Unfold energy to identify the integral function and close the arbitrary positive basepoint. Base integrability in T006 ensures this differentiates the actual finite integral.

steps.statement:
∀ (x : Space n) (t : ℝ), 0 < t →
 dot ((ubar u q) (x,t)) (velocity (ubar u q) x t) = 0 ∧
 dot (velocity (ubar u q) x t) ((ubar u q) (x,t)) = 0
steps.explanation: Differentiate the finite sum of squared coordinates in UnitValued using the actual time derivatives from N001. The function equals 1 locally at every positive time, so its derivative is zero. Divide by 2 and commute real products. This step isolates tangency from normality.

steps.statement:
∀ (x : Space n) (t : ℝ), 0 < t →
 dot ((ubar u q) (x,t)) (velocity (ubar u q) x t) = 0 ∧
 dot (velocity (ubar u q) x t) ((ubar u q) (x,t)) = 0 ∧
 dot (velocity (ubar u q) x t) (acceleration (ubar u q) x t - laplacian (ubar u q) x t) = 0
steps.explanation: Export N004. Select only the pointwise scalar in Normal and substitute A−L=a•ubar into dot(V,A−L). Tangency makes this zero by finite distributivity. Eliminate the witness and close x,t; do not choose or differentiate a witness function.

steps.statement:
∀ t₀ : ℝ, 0 < t₀ → ∀ j : Fin n,
 (∫ x, dot (spatial (ubar u q) j x t₀) (mixed (ubar u q) j x t₀)) =
   -(∫ x, dot (velocity (ubar u q) x t₀) (spatialSecond (ubar u q) j x t₀)) ∧
 Integrable (fun x => dot (spatial (ubar u q) j x t₀) (mixed (ubar u q) j x t₀)) ∧
 Integrable (fun x => dot (velocity (ubar u q) x t₀) (spatialSecond (ubar u q) j x t₀)) ∧
 (∀ k : Fin m,
 Integrable (fun x => velocity (ubar u q) x t₀ k * spatialSecond (ubar u q) j x t₀ k) ∧
 Integrable (fun x => mixed (ubar u q) j x t₀ k * spatial (ubar u q) j x t₀ k) ∧
 Integrable (fun x => velocity (ubar u q) x t₀ k * spatial (ubar u q) j x t₀ k))
steps.explanation: Export N005. Apply the native scalar directional integration-by-parts theorem on Space n with canonical Lebesgue additive Haar measure, direction Pi.single j 1, f=V_k and g=P_j,k. N001 gives differentiability and actual directional derivatives; N002 gives all three product integrability premises. Sum over k using integrability and finite-sum linearity; commute real multiplication to obtain the stated dot-product order. Preserve the auxiliary scalar integrability conclusions.

steps.statement: ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → HasDerivAt (energy (ubar u q)) 0 t
steps.explanation: All terms are integrable by N002. Expand the rate integral into 2∫dot(V,A)+2∑j∫dot(P_j,W_j), substitute N005, and combine the finite sums to get 2∫dot(V,A−L). N004 makes the integrand zero pointwise. Replace the derivative value in N003 by zero.

steps.statement: ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → Integrable (fun x => density (ubar u q) x t) ∧ DifferentiableAt ℝ (energy (ubar u q)) t ∧ deriv (energy (ubar u q)) t = 0
steps.explanation: Export the full P. Combine energy-density integrability from N002 with HasDerivAt E 0 from T011; the latter gives differentiability and deriv E t=0. N001 and the fixed definitions identify the actual Euclidean/Frobenius density and original volume integral, with coefficient 1 on every square and no assertion at zero.

import Mathlib
open scoped Topology ContDiff
open MeasureTheory Filter
namespace WaveMapEnergy
abbrev Space (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ
abbrev Value (m : ℕ) := Fin m → ℝ
def dot {m : ℕ} (v w : Value m) : ℝ := ∑ k, v k * w k
def normSq {m : ℕ} (v : Value m) : ℝ := dot v v
noncomputable def velocity {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
  fun k => deriv (fun r => u (x, r) k) t
noncomputable def acceleration {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
  fun k => deriv (fun r => velocity u x r k) t
noncomputable def spatial {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (j : Fin n) (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
  fun k => fderiv ℝ (fun y => u (y, t) k) x (Pi.single j 1)
noncomputable def spatialSecond {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (j : Fin n) (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
  fun k => fderiv ℝ (fun y => spatial u j y t k) x (Pi.single j 1)
noncomputable def laplacian {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m := ∑ j, spatialSecond u j x t
noncomputable def density {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  normSq (velocity u x t) + ∑ j, normSq (spatial u j x t)
noncomputable def energy {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x, density u x t
def Smooth {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) : Prop :=
  ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ u {p | 0 < p.2}
def UnitValued {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) : Prop :=
  ∀ x t, 0 < t → normSq (u (x, t)) = 1
def Normal {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) : Prop :=
  ∀ x t, 0 < t → ∃ a : ℝ, acceleration u x t - laplacian u x t = a • u (x, t)
def CompactPerturbation {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) (q : Value m) : Prop :=
  ∀ s t : ℝ, 0 < s → s < t → ∃ C : Set (Space n), IsCompact C ∧
    ∀ x r, x ∉ C → r ∈ Set.Icc s t → u (x, r) = q
end WaveMapEnergy

namespace WaveMapEnergy
noncomputable def ubar {n m : ℕ}
    (u : Space n × Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ) → Value m) (q : Value m)
    (p : Space n × ℝ) : Value m :=
  if h : 0 < p.2 then u (p.1, ⟨p.2, h⟩) else q
noncomputable def mixed {n m : ℕ} (v : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (j : Fin n) (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
  fun k => fderiv ℝ (fun y => velocity v y t k) x (Pi.single j 1)
noncomputable def densityRate {n m : ℕ} (v : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  2 * dot (velocity v x t) (acceleration v x t) +
    2 * ∑ j, dot (spatial v j x t) (mixed v j x t)
def FirstCalculus {n m : ℕ} (v : Space n × ℝ → Value m) : Prop :=
  Smooth v ∧
  ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun p : Space n × ℝ => velocity v p.1 p.2) {p | 0 < p.2} ∧
  (∀ j : Fin n, ContDiffOn ℝ ∞
    (fun p : Space n × ℝ => spatial v j p.1 p.2) {p | 0 < p.2}) ∧
  (∀ (x : Space n) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → ∀ k : Fin m,
    HasDerivAt (fun r => v (x,r) k) (velocity v x t k) t) ∧
  (∀ (x : Space n) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → ∀ k : Fin m,
    HasFDerivAt (fun y => v (y,t) k) (fderiv ℝ (fun y => v (y,t) k) x) x)
def SecondCalculus {n m : ℕ} (v : Space n × ℝ → Value m) : Prop :=
  ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun p : Space n × ℝ => acceleration v p.1 p.2) {p | 0 < p.2} ∧
  (∀ j : Fin n, ContDiffOn ℝ ∞
    (fun p : Space n × ℝ => spatialSecond v j p.1 p.2) {p | 0 < p.2}) ∧
  (∀ j : Fin n, ContDiffOn ℝ ∞
    (fun p : Space n × ℝ => mixed v j p.1 p.2) {p | 0 < p.2}) ∧
  (∀ (x : Space n) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → ∀ k : Fin m,
    HasDerivAt (fun r => velocity v x r k) (acceleration v x t k) t) ∧
  (∀ (j : Fin n) (x : Space n) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → ∀ k : Fin m,
    HasDerivAt (fun r => spatial v j x r k) (mixed v j x t k) t) ∧
  (∀ (j : Fin n) (x : Space n) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → ∀ k : Fin m,
    HasFDerivAt (fun y => velocity v y t k)
      (fderiv ℝ (fun y => velocity v y t k) x) x ∧
    HasFDerivAt (fun y => spatial v j y t k)
      (fderiv ℝ (fun y => spatial v j y t k) x) x)
noncomputable def sections {n m : ℕ} (v : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (t : ℝ) : Set (Space n → ℝ) :=
  {h | h = (fun x => density v x t) ∨ h = (fun x => densityRate v x t) ∨
    (∃ k : Fin m, h = (fun x => velocity v x t k) ∨
      h = (fun x => acceleration v x t k) ∨
      h = (fun x => velocity v x t k * acceleration v x t k)) ∨
    (∃ (j : Fin n) (k : Fin m),
      h = (fun x => spatial v j x t k) ∨
      h = (fun x => spatialSecond v j x t k) ∨
      h = (fun x => mixed v j x t k) ∨
      h = (fun x => spatial v j x t k * mixed v j x t k) ∨
      h = (fun x => velocity v x t k * spatialSecond v j x t k) ∨
      h = (fun x => velocity v x t k * spatial v j x t k) ∨
      h = (fun x => mixed v j x t k * spatial v j x t k)) ∨
    h = (fun x => dot (velocity v x t) (acceleration v x t)) ∨
    (∃ j : Fin n,
      h = (fun x => dot (spatial v j x t) (mixed v j x t)) ∨
      h = (fun x => dot (velocity v x t) (spatialSecond v j x t)) ∨
      h = (fun x => dot (velocity v x t) (spatial v j x t)) ∨
      h = (fun x => dot (mixed v j x t) (spatial v j x t)))}
def SupportedSection {n : ℕ} (C : Set (Space n)) (h : Space n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  Continuous h ∧ tsupport h ⊆ C ∧ HasCompactSupport h ∧ Integrable h
def SlabVanishing {n m : ℕ} (v : Space n × ℝ → Value m) (q : Value m)
    (t₀ : ℝ) (C : Set (Space n)) : Prop :=
  IsCompact C ∧
  (∀ x r, x ∉ C → r ∈ Set.Icc (t₀/2) (3*t₀/2) → v (x,r) = q) ∧
  (∀ (ell : ℕ), 0 < ell → ∀ x r,
    x ∉ C → r ∈ Set.Ioo (t₀/2) (3*t₀/2) → iteratedFDeriv ℝ ell v (x,r) = 0) ∧
  (∀ x r, x ∉ C → r ∈ Set.Ioo (t₀/2) (3*t₀/2) →
    velocity v x r = 0 ∧ acceleration v x r = 0 ∧
    (∀ j, spatial v j x r = 0 ∧ spatialSecond v j x r = 0 ∧ mixed v j x r = 0) ∧
    density v x r = 0 ∧ densityRate v x r = 0)
end WaveMapEnergy

P.explanation: Parameters n,m are natural dimensions with H001 enforcing n,m≥1, equivalent to the specified positive integer dimensions. The parameter u has exactly the original positive-time domain in fixed standard coordinates; q is the fixed vector. H002 requires smoothness only on the positive open half-space of its canonical extension ubar, equivalent in both directions to joint smoothness of the original map by restriction and local agreement. H003 and H004 use normSq=∑k v_k²=1, equivalent over ℝ to Euclidean norm 1 since that norm is nonnegative. H005 retains ∀x,t>0 ∃a:ℝ with A−L=a•ubar and imposes no regularity or global choice of a. H006 keeps ∀0<s<t ∃compact C ∀x∉C ∀r∈[s,t], ubar=q, so support remains locally uniform in time. Restricting ubar recovers u and extending u by q recovers ubar; all derivatives at positive times are local and unchanged. Standard coordinate identities preserve the finite-dimensional topology and Fréchet derivatives in both directions, while normSq and finite spatial sums are exactly the Euclidean and Frobenius squares and volume is exactly product Lebesgue measure. The conclusion explicitly quantifies every real t>0 and proves integrability of the coefficient-1 density, DifferentiableAt of its actual energy integral, and deriv=0. Thus the complete target and all hypotheses correspond in both directions; there is no additional assertion at zero, stronger support requirement, or assumption on the scalar witness.

value.statement: For every real t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝⁿ, the finite energy E is differentiable at t, and E'(t)=0. Here e=|u_t|²+∑_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|² and E(t)=∫_{ℝⁿ}e(x,t) dx with Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure; there is no assertion at time zero.

results.value: Preserve the prepared-basis lean_header verbatim. Space n and Value m are standard real coordinate tuples with product norm for their topology and Fréchet calculus; the physical Euclidean square is the explicit finite sum normSq, never the product norm square. The original map parameter u has domain Space n × Set.Ioi 0, and ubar u q extends it by q at nonpositive times exactly as D005. Smooth is ContDiffOn on the open half-space. The smoothness exponent ∞ is ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), strictly distinguished from analytic ω=(⊤ : WithTop ℕ∞). Derivatives are real scalar-coordinate deriv/fderiv and the mixed field uses the same spatial basis Pi.single j 1. iteratedFDeriv ℝ ell denotes the ell-fold continuous multilinear spacetime derivative, ell a positive natural. volume on Fin n→ℝ is canonical coordinate product Lebesgue measure, without scaling. The function-space submodule span encodes exactly finite real linear combinations of the listed sections. FirstCalculus, SecondCalculus, SlabVanishing and SupportedSection merely package explicit propositions, contain no asserted proof, and become available only when their T obligations are proved. No Audit A note is a premise. All M roots are omitted in favor of direct pinned library use; prepared native dependencies have port=null and there are no E roots.

1: # Audit B: endpoint fidelity and checked Lean closure
2: 
3: For the optional [basis route](../../nl0/references/basis.md), this same Audit B
4: checks the conditional intermediate under the frozen basis interfaces. It is
5: followed by b2lean's fresh inspection of the actual `YuiClosed.P`, with only
6: original H and explicitly approved class 4 remaining. Its final receipt binds
7: the compiled standalone source and full actual signature/dependency closure;
8: this intermediate receipt must not be reported as unconditional completion.
9: 
10: The stage-two policy is `endpoint-fidelity-2` (Audit B schema version 2).
11: Its semantic objects are every original external theorem E and the complete
12: final target P. P includes its parameters, quantifiers, hypotheses, domains and
13: conclusion. Accepted NL0/Audit A remains the source authority; B does not repeat
14: unchanged natural-language proof checking.
15: 
16: ## Normal final acceptance and deviation exception
17: 
18: The normal workflow uses `yui-frozen-interface-acceptance-1`. A complete independent
19: pre-proof review establishes source-to-type fidelity for every E and full P and
20: all definitions needed to interpret them. Final native inspection compares the
21: actual exported full types against that frozen contract, checks the exact defining
22: header/pins and semantic receipt, and validates standalone proof/dependency/trust
23: closure. This normal final gate is pure machine work: no additional final LLM is
24: called. It records inherited semantics, not a newly performed independent Audit B.
25: 
26: The actual E/P types include retained hypotheses and quantifiers. Text labels or
27: a source-hash check alone do not establish this gate. The original mathematical
28: review may be wrong; the machine establishes preservation of that reviewed encoding,
29: not correctness of the reviewer's natural-language judgment.
30: 
31: Only complete proof-integrity success plus genuine endpoint/definition drift may
32: open the exceptional independent B-final review below. A faithful result then has
33: `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL`, a freeze-deviation warning and an explicit harness-defect
34: report. Invalid native evidence, incomplete dependencies or changed provenance
35: cannot be overridden semantically. Nonfaithful/unverified results wait for the
36: three explicit user choices in [proof repair](proof-repair.md); accepting a different
37: result does not complete the original target. Explicit/manual legacy semantic
38: receipts remain supported under their original schemas and are not relabeled.
39: Explicitly nonindependent/self-review records remain readable development checks;
40: they cannot grant whole-workflow Audit B acceptance. The same qualification rule
41: applies to supplied Audit A authority and incremental producer/cut reviews.
42: 
43: ## Author correspondence explanations
44: 
45: During interface authoring, provide `endpoint_correspondence`, keyed by every
46: E ID and P. Each entry is `{mode: direct|equivalent, explanation: string}`.
47: Keep it short and useful; do not restate the entire proof or manufacture a
48: line-by-line formalization commentary:
49: 
50: - **Direct:** identify the corresponding variables, hypotheses and assertion.
51:   One sentence is enough when the translation is immediate.
52: - **Equivalent:** explain the mathematical identification or reformulation,
53:   why it works in both directions and which existing conditions it uses.
54:   Point to relevant definitions or checked conversions when needed.
55: 
56: For example, expressing invariance under a finite basis of operators can encode
57: invariance under their linear span: explain the spanning property and closure
58: of a subspace under linear combinations. The review must establish those facts
59: for the actual source algebra/action; the word “equivalent” alone is insufficient.
60: 
61: The postprocessing author carries these notes into each E/P entry in
62: `mapping.json`, checks them against the actual export and completes missing
63: notes for older frozen contracts. It must not change frozen proof statements
64: or bodies merely to improve a note. An explanation is an author's claim, not
65: an Audit B verdict or a formal proof.
66: 
67: ## Semantic responsibility before freeze or at explicit B-final
68: 
69: Read the explanation together with the original source statement and actual
70: elaborated Lean type. Follow the definitions needed to interpret the endpoint,
71: including structure fields that might hide extra assumptions. Check each E/P
72: row, then these four global checks:
73: 
74: 1. `endpoint_inventory_and_scope`: all original E statements and P are covered;
75:    the source version, reviewer scope and inherited qualifications are explicit.
76: 2. `external_statement_fidelity`: each external assumption has the source's
77:    complete mathematical meaning, including conditions and quantifiers. With
78:    no external inputs, record that fact.
79: 3. `complete_target_and_representations`: the entire target theorem has the
80:    same meaning, including every hypothesis. Validate the explanation of each
81:    direct or equivalent encoding and relevant edge cases.
82: 4. `kernel_closure_and_trust`: the actual exported proof compiled, all required
83:    producers and intermediate library ports were discharged, and the checked
84:    root has only the declared external assumptions and permitted foundations.
85: 
86: Equivalent formulations are allowed. Do not reject a faithful encoding because
87: it lacks a particular Mathlib type/name, a separate object for every NL0
88: D node, or a duplicate formal representation. A mathematical source-to-code
89: identification can be checked semantically without constructing an unnecessary
90: second model. If the implementation actually crosses two different Lean
91: representations, the required conversion must occur in checked Lean code.
92: Unexplained equivalence, stronger assumptions, missing hypotheses, changed
93: domains or hidden target assumptions remain defects.
94: 
95: Do not accept an explanation on trust or copy the author's conclusion into the
96: review. Record PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED with specific findings and source/type/note
97: locations. A compiler pass cannot substitute for this independent judgment.
98: 
99: ## Freely available Mathlib
100: 
101: All proved results in the pinned Mathlib environment are available in stage
102: two. Do not compare their names, counts or node-by-node uses with the NL0 M
103: inventory. There is no per-M semantic row, imported-proof whitelist,
104: `calculation_links` ledger, or separate review of implementation N/D nodes.
105: Definitions are examined when they determine endpoint meaning, not for an
106: exact inventory match. Notes from Audit A are optional local guidance, not
107: permissions to use a library theorem.
108: 
109: New interfaces normally use Mathlib directly. An older or deliberately
110: conditional interface can retain M ports; `library_terms` supplies an actual
111: Lean proof for each such port at assembly. These are discharge proofs, not a
112: library correspondence inventory. They cannot remain unproved assumptions of
113: the final export. New external axioms or stronger project hypotheses still
114: require returning to the affected source boundary.
115: 
116: ## Mechanical evidence and limits
117: 
118: ### Compact review materials
119: 
120: The semantic reviewer reads the separately versioned
121: `yui-audit-b-review-view-1` in `review-packet.json`. Start at `/scope` and
122: `/mechanical_summary`, then examine each `/endpoints/<ID>` source, actual
123: inspected type and author correspondence. P retains the complete original
124: target, parameters and hypotheses. The view is a deterministic Python extraction,
125: not an LLM summary or mathematical judgment. It never substitutes a declared
126: expected type for the actual inspected type.
127: 
128: `/documents` identifies hash-bound `source-context.json`, `source-original.txt`
129: and actual `Proof.lean`. Read relevant original and Lean definitions there,
130: including hidden structure fields, when needed to interpret an endpoint.
131: Complete raw compiler, elaboration and dependency records stay in the machine
132: archive; they are not default reviewer inputs. A mechanical summary reports
133: actual checks and exceptions, without populating a semantic PASS. The full
134: dependency inspection remains a program responsibility.
135: 
136: Use `read_task_input` JSON pointers, not guessed fixed line positions. Large
137: containers expose keys and large strings expose `next_offset`. Text reads
138: resume with `next_start` and `next_column`. Serialized read results are at most
139: 32 KiB; follow `has_more` until the needed statement is complete. This pagination
140: limit is not a task time/token/call budget. Unknown calls or modified feedback
141: remain rejected with a specific local protocol fault, not a retryable HTTP 502.
142: 
143: ### Explicit reuse of completed native evidence
144: 
145: `audit_b.py reuse-review <new-directory> --original <old-audit-directory>`
146: prepares a new semantic review without rebuilding or changing Lean. It validates
147: every original input and snapshot, the original native artifacts/output, source
148: and accepted-A authority, environment pins, and the exact historical tool
149: snapshots. The new view and current reviewer runtime are separately bound in
150: `review-reuse.json`; the normal current-build tool check is not disabled.
151: Changed or incomplete evidence blocks reuse. Preserve the original failure.
152: 
153: The new independent reviewer receives no previous B verdict, reviewer history,
154: owner reasoning or other-case material. The receipt discloses inherited native
155: checks and a new semantic review; it cannot claim fresh compilation, an unaided
156: cold whole-workflow success or measured acceleration. Changing proofs or source
157: requires the appropriate new checks, rather than this review-only path.
158: 
159: `audit_b.py prepare/build/check` binds the source, accepted A, contract, plan,
160: proofs, tool versions and environment hashes. Build compiles standalone
161: `Proof.lean` before adding inspection. It checks E/P against their declared
162: encoded types, modulo definitional equality and bijective universe renaming.
163: It does not prove equivalence between natural-language text and Lean.
164: Distinct universes must not be collapsed; changed types or hypotheses must not
165: be normalized away. Source fidelity is established by the bound pre-proof independent review, or an actual exceptional B-final review; this native comparison does not establish it anew.
166: 
167: Inspection follows the actual `AuditBExport.P` closure. No `sorry`, unproved
168: local axiom/opaque substitute or undeclared foundation may be introduced.
169: Local bodies still compile against their own task inputs and the pinned
170: library; every required producer must exist. Assembly, inspection and semantic
171: review have separate recorded outcomes.
172: 
173: Version-1 receipts remain historical results under their original policy.
174: They cannot be silently relabeled or accepted as version-2 reviews. Start a
175: new bound audit when policy, source, code or evidence changes. Pending templates
176: never pass. A whole accepted source plus complete native gates and its bound semantic
177: authority yields `AUDIT-B-PASSED`; a fragment yields at most the explicitly
178: scoped development verdict. A whole source with an actual conditional Audit A
179: can yield `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL` after all the same native and semantic checks.
180: It retains the exact source warnings and never upgrades them to full PASS.
181: Neither proves external publications in Lean or
182: establishes formalizer speedup. Preserve failures and report actual costs.

argument.text: H001 fixes positive finite dimensions. Use the fixed standard coordinates on both original Euclidean spaces. For a vector in any such coordinate space, its maximum coordinate norm is at most its Euclidean norm, and its Euclidean norm is at most the square root of the number of coordinates times its maximum coordinate norm. Thus the coordinate identity and its inverse are continuous linear maps; they preserve Fréchet differentiability and all C∞ orders by the chain rule. The coordinates are the original standard ones, so dot and normSq are exactly the original dot product and squared Euclidean norm, not the product norm squared. Lebesgue measure in these standard coordinates is by definition the product of the usual real coordinate Lebesgue measures, giving dx with no Jacobian or rescaling. Restricting ubar to U recovers u, and conversely extension by q gives the total ubar. At a point of U a neighborhood stays in U, so all derivatives there are local and independent of the extension at nonpositive times. H002 therefore gives C∞ regularity of ubar on U. The derivative definitions, finite coordinate sums and the measure identification give the asserted meanings of V,A,Psp,Ssp,L,e,E once their actual derivative identities are checked below. The derivative of the affine time injection r↦(x,r) sends h to (0,h); the derivative of y↦(y,t) sends h to (h,0). The ordinary chain rule identifies V(x,t)_k=Dw(p)T and Psp(j,x,t)_k=Dw(p)Xdir, first as HasDerivAt or HasFDerivAt assertions, then as equalities by uniqueness. These identities hold on all U, not just at p. Evaluation at a fixed direction is continuous linear, so the identities and smoothness of Dw show that V and every Psp(j) are C∞ on U, componentwise and hence as finite vector-valued maps. In particular the actual time derivative of each coordinate of ubar is V. Record F002 with these first-derivative and smoothness facts.

results.text:
1: # Conservation of energy for a sphere-valued wave map
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Lawrence C. Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, second edition,
6: Graduate Studies in Mathematics 19, AMS, 2010, section 12.6, exercise 14,
7: printed page 694. The preceding exercise 13 defines the sphere-valued
8: wave map. ISBN: 978-0-8218-4974-3.
9: 
10: > 14. Prove that if \(\mathbf u\) is a wave map into the unit sphere,
11: > with compact support in space, we have conservation of energy:
12: > \[
13: > \frac{d}{dt}\int_{\mathbb R^n}
14: >       |\mathbf u_t|^2+|D\mathbf u|^2\,dx=0.
15: > \]
16: 
17: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
18: 
19: A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
20: the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
21: of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
22: This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
23: correction.
24: 
25: Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
26: \(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
27: Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:
28: 
29: 1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
30: 2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
31:    \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
32:    \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
33:    assumed.
34: 3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
35:    \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
36:    \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).
37: 
38: With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define
39: 
40: \[
41: e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
42: \qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
43: \]
44: 
45: The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
46: \(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
47: Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
48: and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
49: 
50: ## Fixed natural-language proof
51: 
52: ### 1. Tangency and the wave-map equation
53: 
54: Differentiate \(u\cdot u=1\) in time. The product rule gives
55: \(2u\cdot u_t=0\), so
56: 
57: \[
58: u\cdot u_t=0,\qquad
59: u_t\cdot(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu)=a(u_t\cdot u)=0.          \tag{1}
60: \]
61: 
62: No derivative of \(a\) is needed. The familiar explicit equation also
63: follows from the assumptions: twice differentiating the unit constraint
64: gives \(u\cdot u_{tt}=-|u_t|^2\) and
65: \(u\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u=-|\partial_{x_j}u|^2\).
66: Dotting the normality equation with \(u\), using \(|u|^2=1\), yields
67: \(a=\sum_j|\partial_{x_j}u|^2-|u_t|^2\). This is a consequence,
68: not an additional PDE assumption.
69: 
70: ### 2. Common compact support and integrability
71: 
72: Fix \(t_0>0\), put \(J=[t_0/2,3t_0/2]\), and choose its compact
73: spatial set \(C\) from assumption 3. Since \(C\) is bounded, choose
74: \(R>0\) with \(C\subset(-R,R)^n\) and set \(Q=[-R,R]^n\).
75: The box has finite Lebesgue measure \((2R)^n\).
76: 
77: On the open set \((\mathbb R^n\setminus C)\times\operatorname{int}J\),
78: the map equals the constant \(q\), so all its positive-order
79: derivatives vanish. At interior times, \(e\), \(e_t\), and the
80: derivative products used below consequently vanish outside \(C\).
81: They are continuous by smoothness; their spatial sections are measurable,
82: bounded on \(Q\), and supported there. Their absolute integrals are
83: bounded by a finite constant times \(|Q|\). This proves integrability
84: of \(e(\cdot,t_0)\) and of all later terms. Since \(t_0\) was arbitrary,
85: the energy is a finite, well-defined integral at every positive time.
86: 
87: ### 3. Differentiate the energy integral
88: 
89: The product rule and equality of mixed derivatives give
90: 
91: \[
92: e_t=2u_t\cdot u_{tt}
93:    +2\sum_{j=1}^n\partial_{x_j}u\cdot\partial_{x_j}u_t.           \tag{2}
94: \]
95: 
96: Choose \(\eta>0\) so that
97: \([t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\subset\operatorname{int}J\).
98: Continuity of (2) on the compact box
99: \(Q\times[t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\) gives a finite bound \(|e_t|\leq B\).
100: For \(0<|h|<\eta\), the one-variable mean value theorem at fixed
101: \(x\) therefore gives
102: 
103: \[
104: \left|\frac{e(x,t_0+h)-e(x,t_0)}h\right|
105: \leq B\mathbf1_Q(x).
106: \]
107: 
108: Outside \(Q\), both densities vanish, so the bound holds throughout
109: \(\mathbb R^n\). The right side is integrable. The difference
110: quotients converge pointwise to \(e_t(x,t_0)\). Dominated convergence
111: and linearity for these integrable functions now prove
112: 
113: \[
114: E'(t_0)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e_t(x,t_0)\,dx.            \tag{3}
115: \]
116: 
117: This establishes differentiability of the actual finite integral.
118: 
119: ### 4. Integration by parts and cancellation
120: 
121: For each spatial index \(j\), at time \(t_0\) put
122: \(g_j(x)=u_t(x,t_0)\cdot\partial_{x_j}u(x,t_0)\).
123: It is smooth and vanishes on a neighborhood of the boundary of \(Q\),
124: because \(C\subset\operatorname{int}Q\). The product rule gives
125: 
126: \[
127: \partial_{x_j}g_j
128: =\partial_{x_j}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_j}u
129:  +u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u.
130: \]
131: 
132: Integrate first over \(x_j\in[-R,R]\) at fixed remaining coordinates.
133: The fundamental theorem of calculus gives zero because both endpoint
134: values of \(g_j\) are zero. Fubini applies on \(Q\) because the
135: derivative and its two summands are continuous and bounded on a
136: finite-measure box. Thus \(\int_Q\partial_{x_j}g_j=0\).
137: All these terms vanish outside \(Q\), so
138: 
139: \[
140: \int_{\mathbb R^n}\partial_{x_j}u\cdot\partial_{x_j}u_t\,dx
141: =-\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u\,dx.              \tag{4}
142: \]
143: 
144: Every integral is finite by step 2. Sum (4) over the finitely many
145: spatial indices and substitute (2) into (3):
146: 
147: \[
148: \begin{aligned}
149: E'(t_0)
150: &=2\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot u_{tt}\,dx
151:  -2\sum_{j=1}^n\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u\,dx\\
152: &=2\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu)\,dx=0,
153: \end{aligned}
154: \]
155: 
156: by (1). This holds at every \(t_0>0\). Hence \(E\) is differentiable
157: with zero derivative on \((0,\infty)\), and is constant there by the
158: mean value theorem. This is conservation of energy with exactly the
159: normalization in the exercise.
160:

1: # Conservation of energy for a sphere-valued wave map
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Lawrence C. Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, second edition,
6: Graduate Studies in Mathematics 19, AMS, 2010, section 12.6, exercise 14,
7: printed page 694. The preceding exercise 13 defines the sphere-valued
8: wave map. ISBN: 978-0-8218-4974-3.
9: 
10: > 14. Prove that if \(\mathbf u\) is a wave map into the unit sphere,
11: > with compact support in space, we have conservation of energy:
12: > \[
13: > \frac{d}{dt}\int_{\mathbb R^n}
14: >       |\mathbf u_t|^2+|D\mathbf u|^2\,dx=0.
15: > \]
16: 
17: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
18: 
19: A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
20: the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
21: of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
22: This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
23: correction.
24: 
25: Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
26: \(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
27: Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:
28: 
29: 1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
30: 2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
31:    \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
32:    \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
33:    assumed.
34: 3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
35:    \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
36:    \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).
37: 
38: With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define
39: 
40: \[
41: e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
42: \qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
43: \]
44: 
45: The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
46: \(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
47: Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
48: and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
49: 
50: ## Fixed natural-language proof
51: 
52: ### 1. Tangency and the wave-map equation
53: 
54: Differentiate \(u\cdot u=1\) in time. The product rule gives
55: \(2u\cdot u_t=0\), so
56: 
57: \[
58: u\cdot u_t=0,\qquad
59: u_t\cdot(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu)=a(u_t\cdot u)=0.          \tag{1}
60: \]
61: 
62: No derivative of \(a\) is needed. The familiar explicit equation also
63: follows from the assumptions: twice differentiating the unit constraint
64: gives \(u\cdot u_{tt}=-|u_t|^2\) and
65: \(u\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u=-|\partial_{x_j}u|^2\).
66: Dotting the normality equation with \(u\), using \(|u|^2=1\), yields
67: \(a=\sum_j|\partial_{x_j}u|^2-|u_t|^2\). This is a consequence,
68: not an additional PDE assumption.
69: 
70: ### 2. Common compact support and integrability
71: 
72: Fix \(t_0>0\), put \(J=[t_0/2,3t_0/2]\), and choose its compact
73: spatial set \(C\) from assumption 3. Since \(C\) is bounded, choose
74: \(R>0\) with \(C\subset(-R,R)^n\) and set \(Q=[-R,R]^n\).
75: The box has finite Lebesgue measure \((2R)^n\).
76: 
77: On the open set \((\mathbb R^n\setminus C)\times\operatorname{int}J\),
78: the map equals the constant \(q\), so all its positive-order
79: derivatives vanish. At interior times, \(e\), \(e_t\), and the
80: derivative products used below consequently vanish outside \(C\).
81: They are continuous by smoothness; their spatial sections are measurable,
82: bounded on \(Q\), and supported there. Their absolute integrals are
83: bounded by a finite constant times \(|Q|\). This proves integrability
84: of \(e(\cdot,t_0)\) and of all later terms. Since \(t_0\) was arbitrary,
85: the energy is a finite, well-defined integral at every positive time.
86: 
87: ### 3. Differentiate the energy integral
88: 
89: The product rule and equality of mixed derivatives give
90: 
91: \[
92: e_t=2u_t\cdot u_{tt}
93:    +2\sum_{j=1}^n\partial_{x_j}u\cdot\partial_{x_j}u_t.           \tag{2}
94: \]
95: 
96: Choose \(\eta>0\) so that
97: \([t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\subset\operatorname{int}J\).
98: Continuity of (2) on the compact box
99: \(Q\times[t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\) gives a finite bound \(|e_t|\leq B\).
100: For \(0<|h|<\eta\), the one-variable mean value theorem at fixed
101: \(x\) therefore gives
102: 
103: \[
104: \left|\frac{e(x,t_0+h)-e(x,t_0)}h\right|
105: \leq B\mathbf1_Q(x).
106: \]
107: 
108: Outside \(Q\), both densities vanish, so the bound holds throughout
109: \(\mathbb R^n\). The right side is integrable. The difference
110: quotients converge pointwise to \(e_t(x,t_0)\). Dominated convergence
111: and linearity for these integrable functions now prove
112: 
113: \[
114: E'(t_0)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e_t(x,t_0)\,dx.            \tag{3}
115: \]
116: 
117: This establishes differentiability of the actual finite integral.
118: 
119: ### 4. Integration by parts and cancellation
120: 
121: For each spatial index \(j\), at time \(t_0\) put
122: \(g_j(x)=u_t(x,t_0)\cdot\partial_{x_j}u(x,t_0)\).
123: It is smooth and vanishes on a neighborhood of the boundary of \(Q\),
124: because \(C\subset\operatorname{int}Q\). The product rule gives
125: 
126: \[
127: \partial_{x_j}g_j
128: =\partial_{x_j}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_j}u
129:  +u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u.
130: \]
131: 
132: Integrate first over \(x_j\in[-R,R]\) at fixed remaining coordinates.
133: The fundamental theorem of calculus gives zero because both endpoint
134: values of \(g_j\) are zero. Fubini applies on \(Q\) because the
135: derivative and its two summands are continuous and bounded on a
136: finite-measure box. Thus \(\int_Q\partial_{x_j}g_j=0\).
137: All these terms vanish outside \(Q\), so
138: 
139: \[
140: \int_{\mathbb R^n}\partial_{x_j}u\cdot\partial_{x_j}u_t\,dx
141: =-\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u\,dx.              \tag{4}
142: \]
143: 
144: Every integral is finite by step 2. Sum (4) over the finitely many
145: spatial indices and substitute (2) into (3):
146: 
147: \[
148: \begin{aligned}
149: E'(t_0)
150: &=2\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot u_{tt}\,dx
151:  -2\sum_{j=1}^n\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u\,dx\\
152: &=2\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu)\,dx=0,
153: \end{aligned}
154: \]
155: 
156: by (1). This holds at every \(t_0>0\). Hence \(E\) is differentiable
157: with zero derivative on \((0,\infty)\), and is constant there by the
158: mean value theorem. This is conservation of energy with exactly the
159: normalization in the exercise.

Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required."

1: import Mathlib
2: open scoped Topology ContDiff
3: open MeasureTheory Filter
4: namespace WaveMapEnergy
5: abbrev Space (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ
6: abbrev Value (m : ℕ) := Fin m → ℝ
7: def dot {m : ℕ} (v w : Value m) : ℝ := ∑ k, v k * w k
8: def normSq {m : ℕ} (v : Value m) : ℝ := dot v v
9: noncomputable def velocity {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
10:     (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
11:   fun k => deriv (fun r => u (x, r) k) t
12: noncomputable def acceleration {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
13:     (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
14:   fun k => deriv (fun r => velocity u x r k) t
15: noncomputable def spatial {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
16:     (j : Fin n) (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
17:   fun k => fderiv ℝ (fun y => u (y, t) k) x (Pi.single j 1)
18: noncomputable def spatialSecond {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
19:     (j : Fin n) (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
20:   fun k => fderiv ℝ (fun y => spatial u j y t k) x (Pi.single j 1)
21: noncomputable def laplacian {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
22:     (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m := ∑ j, spatialSecond u j x t
23: noncomputable def density {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
24:     (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
25:   normSq (velocity u x t) + ∑ j, normSq (spatial u j x t)
26: noncomputable def energy {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
27:   ∫ x, density u x t
28: def Smooth {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) : Prop :=
29:   ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ u {p | 0 < p.2}
30: def UnitValued {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) : Prop :=
31:   ∀ x t, 0 < t → normSq (u (x, t)) = 1
32: def Normal {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) : Prop :=
33:   ∀ x t, 0 < t → ∃ a : ℝ, acceleration u x t - laplacian u x t = a • u (x, t)
34: def CompactPerturbation {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) (q : Value m) : Prop :=
35:   ∀ s t : ℝ, 0 < s → s < t → ∃ C : Set (Space n), IsCompact C ∧
36:     ∀ x r, x ∉ C → r ∈ Set.Icc s t → u (x, r) = q
37: end WaveMapEnergy
38: 
39: namespace WaveMapEnergy
40: noncomputable def ubar {n m : ℕ}
41:     (u : Space n × Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ) → Value m) (q : Value m)
42:     (p : Space n × ℝ) : Value m :=
43:   if h : 0 < p.2 then u (p.1, ⟨p.2, h⟩) else q
44: noncomputable def mixed {n m : ℕ} (v : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
45:     (j : Fin n) (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
46:   fun k => fderiv ℝ (fun y => velocity v y t k) x (Pi.single j 1)
47: noncomputable def densityRate {n m : ℕ} (v : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
48:     (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
49:   2 * dot (velocity v x t) (acceleration v x t) +
50:     2 * ∑ j, dot (spatial v j x t) (mixed v j x t)
51: def FirstCalculus {n m : ℕ} (v : Space n × ℝ → Value m) : Prop :=
52:   Smooth v ∧
53:   ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun p : Space n × ℝ => velocity v p.1 p.2) {p | 0 < p.2} ∧
54:   (∀ j : Fin n, ContDiffOn ℝ ∞
55:     (fun p : Space n × ℝ => spatial v j p.1 p.2) {p | 0 < p.2}) ∧
56:   (∀ (x : Space n) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → ∀ k : Fin m,
57:     HasDerivAt (fun r => v (x,r) k) (velocity v x t k) t) ∧
58:   (∀ (x : Space n) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → ∀ k : Fin m,
59:     HasFDerivAt (fun y => v (y,t) k) (fderiv ℝ (fun y => v (y,t) k) x) x)
60: def SecondCalculus {n m : ℕ} (v : Space n × ℝ → Value m) : Prop :=
61:   ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun p : Space n × ℝ => acceleration v p.1 p.2) {p | 0 < p.2} ∧
62:   (∀ j : Fin n, ContDiffOn ℝ ∞
63:     (fun p : Space n × ℝ => spatialSecond v j p.1 p.2) {p | 0 < p.2}) ∧
64:   (∀ j : Fin n, ContDiffOn ℝ ∞
65:     (fun p : Space n × ℝ => mixed v j p.1 p.2) {p | 0 < p.2}) ∧
66:   (∀ (x : Space n) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → ∀ k : Fin m,
67:     HasDerivAt (fun r => velocity v x r k) (acceleration v x t k) t) ∧
68:   (∀ (j : Fin n) (x : Space n) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → ∀ k : Fin m,
69:     HasDerivAt (fun r => spatial v j x r k) (mixed v j x t k) t) ∧
70:   (∀ (j : Fin n) (x : Space n) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → ∀ k : Fin m,
71:     HasFDerivAt (fun y => velocity v y t k)
72:       (fderiv ℝ (fun y => velocity v y t k) x) x ∧
73:     HasFDerivAt (fun y => spatial v j y t k)
74:       (fderiv ℝ (fun y => spatial v j y t k) x) x)
75: noncomputable def sections {n m : ℕ} (v : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
76:     (t : ℝ) : Set (Space n → ℝ) :=
77:   {h | h = (fun x => density v x t) ∨ h = (fun x => densityRate v x t) ∨
78:     (∃ k : Fin m, h = (fun x => velocity v x t k) ∨
79:       h = (fun x => acceleration v x t k) ∨
80:       h = (fun x => velocity v x t k * acceleration v x t k)) ∨
81:     (∃ (j : Fin n) (k : Fin m),
82:       h = (fun x => spatial v j x t k) ∨
83:       h = (fun x => spatialSecond v j x t k) ∨
84:       h = (fun x => mixed v j x t k) ∨
85:       h = (fun x => spatial v j x t k * mixed v j x t k) ∨
86:       h = (fun x => velocity v x t k * spatialSecond v j x t k) ∨
87:       h = (fun x => velocity v x t k * spatial v j x t k) ∨
88:       h = (fun x => mixed v j x t k * spatial v j x t k)) ∨
89:     h = (fun x => dot (velocity v x t) (acceleration v x t)) ∨
90:     (∃ j : Fin n,
91:       h = (fun x => dot (spatial v j x t) (mixed v j x t)) ∨
92:       h = (fun x => dot (velocity v x t) (spatialSecond v j x t)) ∨
93:       h = (fun x => dot (velocity v x t) (spatial v j x t)) ∨
94:       h = (fun x => dot (mixed v j x t) (spatial v j x t)))}
95: def SupportedSection {n : ℕ} (C : Set (Space n)) (h : Space n → ℝ) : Prop :=
96:   Continuous h ∧ tsupport h ⊆ C ∧ HasCompactSupport h ∧ Integrable h
97: def SlabVanishing {n m : ℕ} (v : Space n × ℝ → Value m) (q : Value m)
98:     (t₀ : ℝ) (C : Set (Space n)) : Prop :=
99:   IsCompact C ∧
100:   (∀ x r, x ∉ C → r ∈ Set.Icc (t₀/2) (3*t₀/2) → v (x,r) = q) ∧
101:   (∀ (ell : ℕ), 0 < ell → ∀ x r,
102:     x ∉ C → r ∈ Set.Ioo (t₀/2) (3*t₀/2) → iteratedFDeriv ℝ ell v (x,r) = 0) ∧
103:   (∀ x r, x ∉ C → r ∈ Set.Ioo (t₀/2) (3*t₀/2) →
104:     velocity v x r = 0 ∧ acceleration v x r = 0 ∧
105:     (∀ j, spatial v j x r = 0 ∧ spatialSecond v j x r = 0 ∧ mixed v j x r = 0) ∧
106:     density v x r = 0 ∧ densityRate v x r = 0)
107: end WaveMapEnergy
108: open WaveMapEnergy

110: namespace Translation
111: set_option autoImplicit false

113: def __signature_T001 : Prop :=
114:   (∀ (n : ℕ) (m : ℕ) (u : Space n × Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ) → Value m) (q : Value m) (h_H001 : 1 ≤ n ∧ 1 ≤ m) (h_H002 : Smooth (ubar u q)), (FirstCalculus (ubar u q)))
115: def __signature_T002 : Prop :=
116:   (∀ (n : ℕ) (m : ℕ) (u : Space n × Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ) → Value m) (q : Value m) (h_T001 : FirstCalculus (ubar u q)), (SecondCalculus (ubar u q)))
117: def __signature_T003 : Prop :=
118:   (∀ (n : ℕ) (m : ℕ) (u : Space n × Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ) → Value m) (q : Value m) (h_T001 : FirstCalculus (ubar u q)) (h_T002 : SecondCalculus (ubar u q)), (FirstCalculus (ubar u q) ∧ SecondCalculus (ubar u q) ∧
119: ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun p : Space n × ℝ => density (ubar u q) p.1 p.2) {p | 0 < p.2} ∧
120: ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun p : Space n × ℝ => densityRate (ubar u q) p.1 p.2) {p | 0 < p.2} ∧

1: # Lean implementation safeguards
2: 
3: Apply these requirements within the accepted NL0 and the fixed Lean interface.
4: They govern implementation, not additional NL0 detail or a weaker Audit B.
5: Use existing library readers and local checking tools; no separate review
6: model, new premise or mandatory lookup of every familiar declaration is needed.
7: 
8: 1. **Check critical library signatures.** Before relying on a critical or
9:    unfamiliar library application, establish its complete type in the pinned
10:    environment, including explicit, implicit and instance binders and all
11:    side conditions. Read the declaration or check a small typed application
12:    when its signature is uncertain. Do not infer the calling convention from
13:    its name or pass an implicit argument as though it were an explicit one.
14:    A previously checked signature in this context need not be looked up again.
15: 2. **Constrain difficult inference.** When coercions or implicit inference
16:    obscure the intended application, give the intermediate fact an explicit
17:    type and supply the relevant named parameters, such as the set, exponent
18:    or ambient space. Prefer this to leaving Lean to discover those choices by
19:    unfolding large definitions. Routine unambiguous arguments can stay
20:    implicit; explicit parameters must preserve the existing target and inputs.
21: 3. **Check conversions before combining them.** When an argument crosses Lean
22:    representations, first establish a small typed conversion fact, then use
23:    it in the main proof. In particular, distinguish `ℝ`, `ℝ≥0` and `ℝ≥0∞`;
24:    check the conversion direction, nonnegativity and any finiteness conditions.
25:    A conversion is not automatically invertible, and matching notation does
26:    not establish equality of differently typed expressions. Reuse a checked
27:    fact when available. Do not invent another representation, a global helper
28:    requirement or an extra hypothesis just to satisfy this instruction.
29: 4. **Isolate an inference failure.** If compiler feedback identifies a library
30:    application, coercion or expensive inference problem, reduce the next check
31:    to that application or conversion with explicit local types before adding
32:    more proof code. Use `check_auxiliary` in a proof worker, or
33:    `check_lean_types` during preparation when that tool is supplied. Helpers
34:    use only the current allowed inputs and never become new premises. Once
35:    the small check succeeds, integrate the result and recheck the complete
36:    obligation; success of a helper alone does not accept the target.
37: 
38: 5. **Repair after a bounded check.** Native checks have a separate per-call wall
39:    limit, normally 180 seconds, and use the controller-owned 20,000,000 heartbeat budget.
40:    A timeout or heartbeat diagnostic leaves the goal unaccepted and returns
41:    control to the same worker. Inspect the retained candidate and diagnostic,
42:    then check a smaller typed application, conversion or proof fragment before
43:    integrating it. Do not repeat the unchanged expensive candidate or disable
44:    limits to avoid diagnosis. Preserve the target, allowed inputs and proof
45:    requirements; a timeout alone establishes no mathematical gap.
46: 
47: The runtime enforces the per-call wall limit independently of these writing
48: rules. Whole-case and model-stage execution remain unlimited by default.
49: Retain failed attempts and actual diagnostics. Standalone assembly, native
50: trust/signature checks and final machine Audit B remain required.
51: 
52: Before freeze, every complete T declaration must elaborate with exactly its
53: worker parameters, instances and direct inputs. Explicitly supply parameters
54: that their argument types cannot determine; a same-named context variable is
55: not an inference rule. The strict declaration check defines the proposition,
56: without proving it, and rejects unresolved holes and non-proposition goals.
57: `#check` is a useful reader aid, not sufficient declaration acceptance. A proof
58: body cannot resolve a hole in its preceding theorem declaration.
59: 
60: Checked auxiliary propositions receive a `yui_aux_...` name and an explicit
61: application with the existing local parameters/inputs. Reuse these theorems in
62: later auxiliary checks and the final body. The controller retains their actual
63: proof bodies and compiles them into standalone assembly. They are same-node
64: implementation lemmas, not extra assumptions. Read the helper index after a
65: context reset; never rebuild a checked helper merely because a turn ended.
66: 
67: Separate diagnostic printing from proving. `show_term` and similar suggestion
68: output may spend substantial time after the proof tactic runs. If that diagnostic
69: wrapper is implicated, check the same proof without it; only the new successful
70: check establishes acceptance. Do not ignore an unsuccessful process exit. If
71: small helpers pass but a monolithic body exhausts resources, retain the separate
72: checked helper declarations and compose them rather than repeatedly copying
73: their bodies into a growing proof.

import Mathlib
open scoped Topology ContDiff
open MeasureTheory Filter
namespace WaveMapEnergy
abbrev Space (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ
abbrev Value (m : ℕ) := Fin m → ℝ
def dot {m : ℕ} (v w : Value m) : ℝ := ∑ k, v k * w k
def normSq {m : ℕ} (v : Value m) : ℝ := dot v v
noncomputable def velocity {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
  fun k => deriv (fun r => u (x, r) k) t
noncomputable def acceleration {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
  fun k => deriv (fun r => velocity u x r k) t
noncomputable def spatial {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (j : Fin n) (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
  fun k => fderiv ℝ (fun y => u (y, t) k) x (Pi.single j 1)
noncomputable def spatialSecond {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (j : Fin n) (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m :=
  fun k => fderiv ℝ (fun y => spatial u j y t k) x (Pi.single j 1)
noncomputable def laplacian {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : Value m := ∑ j, spatialSecond u j x t
noncomputable def density {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m)
    (x : Space n) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  normSq (velocity u x t) + ∑ j, normSq (spatial u j x t)
noncomputable def energy {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x, density u x t
def Smooth {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) : Prop :=
  ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ u {p | 0 < p.2}
def UnitValued {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) : Prop :=
  ∀ x t, 0 < t → normSq (u (x, t)) = 1
def Normal {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) : Prop :=
  ∀ x t, 0 < t → ∃ a : ℝ, acceleration u x t - laplacian u x t = a • u (x, t)
def CompactPerturbation {n m : ℕ} (u : Space n × ℝ → Value m) (q : Value m) : Prop :=
  ∀ s t : ℝ, 0 < s → s < t → ∃ C : Set (Space n), IsCompact C ∧
    ∀ x r, x ∉ C → r ∈ Set.Icc s t → u (x, r) = q
end WaveMapEnergy

value.text: H001 fixes positive finite dimensions. Use the fixed standard coordinates on both original Euclidean spaces. For a vector in any such coordinate space, its maximum coordinate norm is at most its Euclidean norm, and its Euclidean norm is at most the square root of the number of coordinates times its maximum coordinate norm. Thus the coordinate identity and its inverse are continuous linear maps; they preserve Fréchet differentiability and all C∞ orders by the chain rule. The coordinates are the original standard ones, so dot and normSq are exactly the original dot product and squared Euclidean norm, not the product norm squared. Lebesgue measure in these standard coordinates is by definition the product of the usual real coordinate Lebesgue measures, giving dx with no Jacobian or rescaling. Restricting ubar to U recovers u, and conversely extension by q gives the total ubar. At a point of U a neighborhood stays in U, so all derivatives there are local and independent of the extension at nonpositive times. H002 therefore gives C∞ regularity of ubar on U. The derivative definitions, finite coordinate sums and the measure identification give the asserted meanings of V,A,Psp,Ssp,L,e,E once their actual derivative identities are checked below. Record F001: this coordinate representation, measure and norm identification is faithful, and ubar is C∞ on U.

Fix arbitrary x∈Space and t>0, with j,k as declared and put p=(x,t), w(y,r)=ubar(y,r)_k, T=(0,1), Xdir=(basis(j),0). F001 and continuous linear scalar projection give w C∞ on the open set U. Apply M006 over ℝ, with domain Space×ℝ, scalar codomain and both smoothness orders ∞: ∞+1=∞ supplies the order inequality, so Dw is C∞ on U. The derivative of the affine time injection r↦(x,r) sends h to (0,h); the derivative of y↦(y,t) sends h to (h,0). The ordinary chain rule identifies V(x,t)_k=Dw(p)T and Psp(j,x,t)_k=Dw(p)Xdir, first as HasDerivAt or HasFDerivAt assertions, then as equalities by uniqueness. These identities hold on all U, not just at p. Evaluation at a fixed direction is continuous linear, so the identities and smoothness of Dw show that V and every Psp(j) are C∞ on U, componentwise and hence as finite vector-valued maps. In particular the actual time derivative of each coordinate of ubar is V. Record F002 with these first-derivative and smoothness facts.

Put Hess(v,w0)=D(Dw)(p)(v)(w0). Apply M006 again, this time to the C∞ map Dw with its continuous-linear-map codomain, and iterate for higher derivatives as needed; U is open and the ∞ order inequality remains valid. Differentiate the fixed evaluations from S002 by the chain rule. This gives ∂_t Psp(j,x,t)_k=Hess(T,Xdir), ∂_j V(x,t)_k=Hess(Xdir,T), A(x,t)_k=Hess(T,T), and Ssp(j,x,t)_k=Hess(Xdir,Xdir). F001 gives C² regularity of w at p because p∈U. Apply M005 over ℝ at order 2, where minSmoothness(ℝ,2)=2, to get Hess(T,Xdir)=Hess(Xdir,T). By the definition of W the common value is W(j,x,t)_k. The same derivative closure and fixed evaluations show A,Ssp(j),W(j) C∞ on U; this holds at every positive point and for every coordinate. Record F003: the full second-derivative regularity and the actual time derivative identities for V and Psp.
